# CLI reference

Every command of the `research` CLI, with its own `--help` text. Regenerate with:

```bash
uv run python docs/guide/gen_cli_reference.py
```

Two options recur and are not repeated in prose below:

* `--workspace` / `-w` — the workspace root. Without it a command reads
  `RESEARCH_WORKSPACE`, then walks up from the current directory looking for
  `research.yaml`.
* `--json` — print the result as JSON instead of text. The JSON is the scriptable
  interface; the text is for reading.

A command that fails prints one `error: ...` line on stderr and exits 1.

#### `research claim audit`

```text

 Usage: research claim audit [OPTIONS] {claim}

 Audit a claim and record what the evidence allows (`claim.audit`).

 Prints the maximum defensible wording, the allowed scope beside the requested one, the
 support, qualifiers and counter-evidence the audit read, the relations it proposes
 reclassifying, its independence and coverage doubts, and any provider disagreement. An
 audit can only lower the ceiling; raising it takes `research claim override`.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    claim      <str>  Claim to audit (C####). [required]                            │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest research.yaml   │
│                              above the current directory.                            │
│                              [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                           │
│ --provider           <str>   Provider entry from `providers:` in research.yaml, or   │
│                              'scripted' with --script.                               │
│ --script             <path>  JSON responses for the scripted provider: a list, or an │
│                              object keyed by role.                                   │
│ --durable                    Run the audit as a resumable, checkpointed workflow.    │
│ --json                       Print the result as JSON instead of text.               │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

```text
│                                synthesis, recommendation.                            │
│                                [default: descriptive]                                │
│ --scope                <str>   Claim scope ladder level: L0-L4, or its name (e.g.    │
│                                corpus_pattern).                                      │
│                                [default: L0]                                         │

│ --predicate            <str>   Proposition predicate.                                │
│ --object               <str>   Proposition object.                                   │
│ --qualifier            <str>   Proposition qualifier as key=value; repeatable.       │
```

#### `research claim override`

```text

 Usage: research claim override [OPTIONS] {claim}

 Overrule the claim auditor, visibly (`claim.override_strength`).

 The override is a Decision first: the recommendation it overrides, the scope chosen
 instead, and the reason are recorded and accepted before the claim moves, and
 everything
 resting on the old ceiling is marked stale rather than rewritten (Product 38,
 ADR-008).

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    claim      <str>  Claim to override (C####). [required]                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest research.yaml   │
│                              above the current directory.                            │
│                              [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                           │
│ --scope              <str>   Claim scope ladder level: L0-L4, or its name (e.g.      │
│                              corpus_pattern).                                        │
│                              [default: L0]                                           │
│ --rationale          <str>   Why the auditor's ceiling is being overruled.           │
│ --json                       Print the result as JSON instead of text.               │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

#### `research claim relate`

```text

 Usage: research claim relate [OPTIONS] {claim} {evidence} {relation}

 Link evidence to a claim (`claim.relate`).

 Relations are many-to-many: the same evidence may support one aspect of a claim and

│ *    evidence      <str>  Evidence to link (E####). [required]                       │
│ *    relation      <str>  Relation: supports, contradicts, qualifies,                │
│                           contextualizes, exemplifies,                               │
│                           incomparable_under_current_evidence.                       │
│                           [required]                                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest research.yaml   │
│                              above the current directory.                            │
│                              [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                           │
│ --aspect             <str>   Aspect of the claim this relation is about.             │
│ --note               <str>   Why the evidence relates this way.                      │
│ --json                       Print the result as JSON instead of text.               │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

### `research compare`

```text

 Usage: research compare [OPTIONS] {field}

 Show one field across every work: labels, the evidence behind them, and the gaps.

 A work with no labels is *unclassified*, which is a statement about the record and
 never about the work: absence needs its own coverage and evidence (Product 11).
```

### `research coverage`

```text

 Usage: research coverage [OPTIONS] {claim}

 Audit a claim's search coverage, record it, and say what wording it permits.

 The funnel this computes is written onto the Claim through `claim.update_coverage`,
 which is where `research claim audit` reads it: two commands computing the same
 quantity and disagreeing is what capped every literature-wide claim at L1 (dogfood
 F2).
 `--dry-run` prints the funnel and records nothing.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    claim      <str>  Claim to audit (C####). [required]                            │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  --universe                   <str>   What the coverage is measured against.       │
│                                         [required]                                   │
│ *  --cutoff                     <str>   Publication cutoff, YYYY-MM. [required]      │
│    --workspace          -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest      │
│                                         research.yaml above the current directory.   │
│                                         [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                │
│    --source                     <str>   Source the universe declares; repeatable.    │
│    --matrix-cell-empty                  An empty synthesis cell prompted this claim. │
│    --models-agree                       Models agreed the property is absent.        │
│    --dry-run                            Print the funnel without recording it on the │
│                                         Claim.                                       │
│    --json                               Print the result as JSON instead of text.    │
│    --help                               Show this message and exit.                  │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

### `research demo`

```text

 Usage: research demo [OPTIONS] {directory}

 Create a workspace with verified proposals waiting for review — offline, no API key.

 Ingests and parses the bundled synthetic paper, stages three proposals with the
 scripted provider, verifies them, and rebuilds the projection. Nothing is accepted:
 that is the researcher's step, in the cockpit (`research serve`), the CLI
 (`research inbox`, `research review`), or an MCP host.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    directory      <path>  Directory to create the demo workspace in (must not      │
│                             exist).                                                  │
│                             [required]                                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --name        <str>  Project name. [default: demo]                                   │
│ --json               Print the result as JSON instead of text.                       │
│ --help               Show this message and exit.                                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

### `research inbox`

```text

 Usage: research inbox [OPTIONS]

 The review queue in Product §24.2 order: conflicts first, routine last.

 Only the first `--limit` items are printed. The header says how many of how many, and
 `--limit 0` prints the whole queue: a researcher working the list top to bottom must
 never be able to believe they cleared it when they cleared a page of it (dogfood F8).

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>              Workspace root; defaults to the nearest     │
│                                          research.yaml above the current directory.  │
│                                          [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]               │
│ --work               <str>               Only this Work (W####).                     │
│ --category           <str>               Only one category: conflict, high_risk,     │
```

### `research interrogate`

```text

 Usage: research interrogate [OPTIONS] {work}

 Ask a Work the interrogation schema's questions; every answer lands in staging.

 Nothing here can change accepted state: candidates are proposals with a source anchor
 and no authority until a researcher accepts them (Product §8.3).

╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

│ --workspace     -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest              │

│                                 [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                        │
│ --provider              <str>   Provider entry from `providers:` in research.yaml,   │
│                                 or 'scripted' with --script.                         │
│ --script                <path>  JSON responses for the scripted provider: a list, or │
│                                 an object keyed by role.                             │
│ --field                 <str>   Field(s) to ask: repeatable, and comma-separated     │
│                                 (`--field dataset,baseline`).                        │
│ --except-field          <str>   Ask every field of the schema except these;          │
│                                 repeatable and comma-separated.                      │
│ --schema                <str>   Interrogation schema: a built-in name,               │
│                                 `plugin:<plugin-name>[:<schema>]` for a domain       │
│                                 plugin's questions, or a path to a JSON file.        │
│ --artifact              <str>   Interrogate this artifact (A####).                   │
│ --rerun                         Re-run every stage instead of reusing checkpoints.   │
│ --json                          Print the result as JSON instead of text.            │
│ --help                          Show this message and exit.                          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

#### `research review batch`

```text

 Usage: research review batch [OPTIONS]

 Accept every candidate meeting the deterministic conditions of Product §24.4.

 Refused outright unless the workspace's `review_policy` is `policy_batch`: strict
 review
 is the default, and a batch is an exception a researcher declares in `research.yaml`
 (ADR-007). Model confidence is never one of the conditions.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest research.yaml   │
│                              above the current directory.                            │
│                              [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                           │
│ --work               <str>   Only this Work (W####).                                 │
│ --dry-run                    Report what would be accepted; change nothing.          │
│ --json                       Print the result as JSON instead of text.               │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

#### `research review candidate`

```text

 Usage: research review candidate [OPTIONS] {candidate_id}

 Show one review item, or answer it. Exactly one action, and the researcher takes it.

 **With no action flag this prints the item** — its verdict, the discrepancies the
 verifier recorded, the competing answers, and the source span with the text around it
 —
 so an honest rejection costs one command rather than a JSON blob in another window
 (dogfood F12).

 **This command is the human gate.** It is the researcher acting in person, so it
 accepts
 any tier, an interpretive candidate included; that is what a review gate is *for*. The
 conditions live on `research review batch`, which is refused outright unless the
 project
 declares `review_policy: policy_batch` and which never accepts a Tier-2 candidate
 (Product §24.4, ADR-007, §42 H). What is refused here is an actor that is not the
 researcher — a model or an agent host reaching the same capability over MCP.

 `--split` is partial acceptance (Product §24.3): the source fact is accepted with the
 candidate's own anchor, and the reading attached to it is either staged as its own
 Tier-2 candidate (`--interpretation`) or refused with a reason
 (`--reject-interpretation`). Exactly one accepted Evidence results either way.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    candidate_id      <str>  Staged candidate id (cand_<16 hex>). [required]        │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace              -w      <path>  Workspace root; defaults to the nearest     │
│                                          research.yaml above the current directory.  │
│                                          [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]               │
│ --accept                                 Accept as canonical Evidence.               │
│ --qualify                        <str>   Accept with an explicit qualification.      │
│ --edit                           <path>  Accept a corrected Evidence read from this  │
│                                          JSON file.                                  │
│ --reject                         <str>   Refuse the candidate, with a reason.        │
│ --defer                          <str>   Put it aside, with a note.                  │
│ --request-more                   <str>   Ask for more evidence; captured as a note.  │
│ --split                                  Accept the source fact and deal with its    │
│                                          interpretation separately.                  │
│ --interpretation                 <str>   With --split: stage this reading for its    │
│                                          own review.                                 │
│ --reject-interpretation          <str>   With --split: refuse the reading, with a    │
│                                          reason.                                     │
│ --json                                   Print the result as JSON instead of text.   │
│ --help                                   Show this message and exit.                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

### `research shell`

```text

 Usage: research shell [OPTIONS]

 Run many commands in one process, so the interpreter is started once.

 Importing the harness costs about a second, and the review loop is dozens of commands:
 the dogfood session spent roughly 80 of 90 seconds importing rather than reviewing
 (dogfood F20). `research serve` already avoids that for a host; this is the same
 saving for the documented path, the CLI.

 Nothing else changes. Each line is dispatched through exactly the same Typer
 application in the same standalone mode a terminal uses, so every command behaves,
 prints, and refuses identically — the shell is a loop around the entry point, not a
 second entry point. State is not carried between commands either: each one opens the
 workspace itself, so a shell session and the same commands typed separately leave the
 same workspace behind. Like a shell, the session exits with the status of the last
 command it ran, so a piped script still fails loudly.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Workspace every command in this session defaults to.    │
│                              [env var: RESEARCH_WORKSPACE]                           │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```
